documents.text:
The `AllowCredentials` option indicates whether the response to the request can be exposed when the credentials flag is true. If `AllowCredentials` is set to `true`, the middleware adds the header `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` to the response. To prevent security vulnerabilities, `AllowCredentials` cannot be set to `true` if `AllowOrigins` is set to a wildcard (`*`).

The `ExposeHeaders` option defines an allowlist of headers that clients are allowed to access. If `ExposeHeaders` is set to `"X-Custom-Header"`, the middleware adds the header `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Custom-Header` to the response.

The `MaxAge` option indicates how long the results of a preflight request can be cached. If `MaxAge` is set to `3600`, the middleware adds the header `Access-Control-Max-Age: 3600` to the response.

The `Vary` header helps caches store the correct response. For simple requests the middleware sets `Vary: Origin` unless all origins are allowed. When all origins are allowed, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (and `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`) is static and is also sent in response to requests without an `Origin` header, `OPTIONS` excepted, so any stored response can be reused for a cross-origin request. Preflight responses add `Vary: Origin, Access-Control-Request-Method, Access-Control-Request-Headers` (and `Access-Control-Request-Private-Network` when enabled and requested). This ensures caches know when to reuse a response and when to revalidate with the server.

#### Updated Struct Fields

We've updated several fields from a single string (containing comma-separated values) to slices, allowing for more explicit declaration of multiple values. Here are the updated fields:

- `Config.AllowOrigins`: Now accepts a slice of strings, each representing an allowed origin.
- `Config.AllowMethods`: Now accepts a slice of strings, each representing an allowed method.
- `Config.AllowHeaders`: Now accepts a slice of strings, each representing an allowed header.
- `Config.ExposeHeaders`: Now accepts a slice of strings, each representing an exposed header.

Additionally, the panic for an invalid `AllowOrigins` entry redacts the origin by default, and a `DisableValueRedaction` flag (default `false`) lets you reveal it when necessary.

When all origins are allowed (the default), `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` is also sent on responses to requests without `Origin`, `OPTIONS` excepted, so a cache in front of the middleware cannot hand a response without it to a cross-origin request.

An IPv6 host in `AllowOrigins` is written in the form browsers send in `Origin`, so `http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:3000` matches `Origin: http://[::1]:3000`.

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
